transformations.edit: Extracted the target-local RChunksMut representation with private `v`, `chunk_size`, and `_marker` fields, preserving field names, order, and privacy while omitting Rust stability/doc attributes.

Represented the Rust `v: *mut [T]` storage as a mutable-slice sequence view in the harness so the generated iterator-view vocabulary can mention the remaining reverse mutable region; raw pointer provenance and aliasing remain an explicit boundary.
Included RChunksMut::new with the real Rust body `Self { v: slice, chunk_size: size, _marker: PhantomData }` so the target call is checked rather than trusted.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains assert then RChunksMut::new(slice, chunk_size).
Adapted the Rust `pub const fn` target item to a non-const Verus harness function; no executable control-flow or data-flow step was changed.
Adapted the private Rust `pub(super) const fn` constructor to a non-const Verus harness function; no executable control-flow or data-flow step was changed.
Converted Rust `assert!(chunk_size != 0, ...)` to Verus `assert(chunk_size != 0)` under the same generated precondition; no control-flow path is removed.
Defined the closed iterator-view helper from the extracted mutable region and chunk size to expose source, remaining, empty yielded prefix/remainder, requested chunk size, and reverse direction.
Revealed the closed iterator-view definition in a ghost proof block; this has no executable data-flow or evaluation-order effect.
Actual Verus verifies the executable source-backed harness after the repaired generated contract removed the unsound final(slice)@ == old(slice)@ frame.
